edition: SPI Napoleon at Waterloo, SECOND EDITION, copyright 1971
authority: PRIMARY. Machine-readable capture of the Combat Resolution Table printed on the folio map sheet (page 5). The CRT had been transcribed cell by cell in PREP-1/PREP-2 but only ever into prose in RULEBOOK_VERIFIED.md; nothing downstream could consume it. This file is that transcription made machine-readable AND independently re-read off the print a fourth time during PREP-5 collation.

source.render: embedded page image at native 6952x5171, no resample
source.block: Combat Resolution Table, French-side copy, printed at 270 degrees
source.note: The sheet prints TWO copies, one per player; PREP-1 read both and they agree cell for cell.

verification.method: all 60 cells re-read BY EYE off three rotated crops regenerated by this script, then compared against RULEBOOK_VERIFIED.md section 3
verification.verdict: EXACT MATCH. The prose transcription is confirmed; no cell changed.
verification.caveat: This is a fourth reading of the SAME printed artefact, not a new witness. It defends against transcription drift between the doc and the data, not against a misprint in the folio itself.

result_codes.EX: Exchange - the defender is eliminated and the attacker suffers a loss AT LEAST EQUAL in Strength Points, made up only from units directly involved in that attack

result_code_note: PREP-2 E04: the 3rd Edition renames these Ae/Ee/De. It is a RENAME, not a rules change - map them, never branch on them.
clamp_printed_verbatim: Attacks executed at worse than “1 to 5” are treated as “1 to 5”; attacks executed at greater than “6 to 1” are treated as “6 to 1”.
clamp_read: by-eye, footnote visible in zz_crt_full and zz_crt_left

odds_rounding.rule: Attacker's total Combat Strength vs defender's total, expressed as a ratio and ROUNDED OFF IN FAVOUR OF THE DEFENDER

consumers: the printed Examples of Attacks (folio p.2) are the validation corpus - every printed example must resolve to its printed odds and result against this table
